arxiv-1812-06802.title: Cornell Potential: A Neural Network Approach
arxiv-1812-06802.creator: Halil Mutuk
arxiv-1812-06802.description: Abstract In this study, we solved Schrödinger equation with Cornell potential (Coulomb-plus-linear potential) by using neural network approach. Four different cases of Cornell Potential for different potential parameters were used without a physical relevance. Besides that charmonium, bottomonium and bottom-charmed spin-averaged spectra were also calculated. Obtained results are in good agreement with the reference studies and available experimental data.

arxiv-2103-09948.title: Physically inspired deep learning of molecular excitations and quasiparticle spectra
arxiv-2103-09948.creator: Julia Westermayr, Reinhard J. Maurer
arxiv-2103-09948.description: Abstract Modern functional materials consist of large molecular building blocks with significant chemical complexity which limits spectroscopic property prediction with accurate first-principles methods. Consequently, a targeted design of materials with tailored optoelectronic properties by high-throughput screening is bound to fail without efficient methods to predict molecular excited-state properties across chemical space.

arxiv-2110-13020.title: Deterministic particle flows for constraining SDEs
arxiv-2110-13020.creator: Dimitra Maoutsa, Manfred Opper
arxiv-2110-13020.description: Abstract Devising optimal interventions for diffusive systems often requires the solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, a nonlinear backward partial differential equation (PDE), that is, in general, nontrivial to solve. Existing control methods either tackle the HJB directly with grid-based PDE solvers, or resort to iterative stochastic path sampling to obtain the necessary controls.

arxiv-2409-20094.title: Aggressive Post-Training Compression on Extremely Large Language Models
arxiv-2409-20094.creator: Zining Zhang, Yao Chen, Bingsheng He, Zhenjie Zhang
arxiv-2409-20094.description: Abstract The increasing size and complexity of Large Language Models (LLMs) pose challenges for their deployment on personal computers and mobile devices. Aggressive post-training model compression is necessary to reduce the models’ size, but it often results in significant accuracy loss. To address this challenge, we propose a novel network pruning technology that utilizes over 0.

arxiv-2501-04156.title: AdaptiveCoPilot: Design and Testing of a NeuroAdaptive LLM Cockpit Guidance System in both Novice and Expert Pilots
arxiv-2501-04156.creator: Shaoyue Wen New York University, Michael Middleton* New York University & Northrop Grumman, Songming Ping Imperial college, Nayan N Chawla Virginia Tech, Guande Wu New York University, Bradley S Feest Northrop Grumman, Chihab Nadri University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign, Yunmei Liu University of L
arxiv-2501-04156.description: Abstract Pilots operating modern cockpits often face high cognitive demands due to complex interfaces and multitasking requirements, which can lead to overload and decreased performance. This study introduces AdaptiveCoPilot , a neuroadaptive guidance system that adapts visual, auditory, and textual cues in real time based on the pilot’s cognitive workload, measured via functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS).

arxiv-2501-12973.title: A global similarity correction for the RANS modeling of natural convection in unstably stratified flows
arxiv-2501-12973.creator: Da-Sol Joo
arxiv-2501-12973.description: Abstract This study proposes a global similarity correction for Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) modeling of buoyancy effects in unstably stratified flows. Conventional two-equation RANS models (e.g., the k k - ε \varepsilon model) lack a clear criterion for incorporating unstable buoyancy effects in their scale-determining equations (e.g., ε \varepsilon -equation).

arxiv-2507-07335.title: Leveraging Manifold Embeddings for Enhanced Graph Transformer Representations and Learning
arxiv-2507-07335.description: Abstract Graph transformers typically embed every node in a single Euclidean space, blurring heterogeneous topologies. We prepend a lightweight Riemannian mixture-of-experts layer that routes each node to various kinds of manifold, mixture of spherical, flat, hyperbolic—best matching its local structure. These projections provide intrinsic geometric explanations to the latent space.

arxiv-2511-12923.title: Fast Quantum Many Body State Synthesis
arxiv-2511-12923.creator: Prashasti Tiwari, Dylan Lewis, Sougato Bose
arxiv-2511-12923.description: Abstract Quantum Mechanical ground states of many-body systems can be important resources for various investigations: for quantum sensing, as the initial state for nonequilibrium quantum dynamics following quenches, and the simulation of quantum processes that start by coupling systems in ground states, eg, could be a process in quantum chemistry.

plos-pone-0002590.description: PLOS ONE research article. Psychophysical studies suggest that humans preferentially use a narrow band of low spatial frequencies for face recognition. Here we asked whether artificial face recognition systems have an improved recognition performance at the same spatial frequencies as humans. To this end,

pmc-10585530.title: Application of ultrasound-based radiomics models of breast masses to predict invasive components of encapsulated papillary carcinoma
pmc-10585530.creator: Jin Zhou, Chaoxu Liu, Zhaoting Shi, Xiaokang Li, Cai Chang, Wenxiang Zhi, Shichong Zhou
pmc-10585530.description: BackgroundAxillary lymph node (ALN) metastasis is seen in encapsulated papillary carcinoma (EPC), mostly with an invasive component (INV). Radiomics can offer more information beyond subjective grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound (US) image interpretation. This study aimed to develop radiomics models for predicting an INV of EPC in the breast based on US images.

pmc-11371589.title: Association between apolipoprotein C-III levels and coronary calcification detected by intravascular ultrasound in patients who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention
pmc-11371589.creator: Tatsuya Fukase, Tomotaka Dohi, Ryota Nishio, Mitsuhiro Takeuchi, Norihito Takahashi, Yuichi Chikata, Hirohisa Endo, Shinichiro Doi, Hiroki Nishiyama, Iwao Okai, Hiroshi Iwata, Seiji Koga, Shinya Okazaki, Katsumi Miyauchi, Hiroyuki Daida, Tohru Minamino
pmc-11371589.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). There are few reports on the association between apolipoprotein C-III (ApoC-III) and coronary calcification using intravascular modalities. This study aimed to investigate the impacts of ApoC-III levels on coronary calcification using grayscale intravascular ultrasound (IVUS). Consecutive 263 culprit lesions for 202 patients who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention using grayscale IVUS were included in this study and divided into four groups based on quartile ApoC-III values.

pmc-11403130.title: Edaravone: A Possible Treatment for Acute Lung Injury
pmc-11403130.creator: Ma Huang, Yalan Mo, Haiyun Lei, Miao Chen
pmc-11403130.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Despite technological advances in science and medicine, acute lung injury (ALI) is still associated with high mortality rates in the ICU. Therefore, finding novel drugs and treatment approaches is crucial to preventing ALI. Drug repurposing is a common practice in clinical research, primarily for drugs that have previously received approval for use in patients, to investigate novel uses of drugs and therapies.

pmc-11447358.title: Bilateral ovarian artery embolization for a symptomatic large cervical fibroid
pmc-11447358.creator: William D Denton, Merve Ozen
pmc-11447358.description: Uterine leiomyomas are one of the most common smooth muscle tumors in women. Cervical leiomyomas, in contrast, are a relatively rare entity with limited available information, presenting a challenge for determining optimal treatment. Uterine artery embolization of cervical leiomyomas has been previously explored and met with some success.

pmc-11640061.title: Effect of Dietary Cold-Pressed Hempseed Cake Supplemented with Tomato Waste on Laying Hen Performance and Egg Yolk Lipid Profile and Antioxidant Status Before and After Storage
pmc-11640061.creator: Daniel Mierlita, Stelian Daraban, Alin Cristian Teușdea, Alina Stefania Stanciu, Sylwester Świątkiewicz
pmc-11640061.description: Simple SummaryPhytochemicals in tomato waste are known for their high antioxidant activity, and carotenoid pigments can be harnessed as natural egg yolk pigments. Also, hempseed cake (HSC) has been recognized as a valuable source of protein and essential fatty acids for poultry nutrition.

pmc-12729644.title: Ecological Succession of Airborne Bacterial Aerosols in Poultry Houses: Insights from Taihang Chickens
pmc-12729644.creator: Yejin Yang, Huan Cui, Zitong Yang, Zhenyue Li, Wenhao Feng, Zhuhua Liu, Mengxi Yan, Zhibin Ren, Ran Zhu, Yuqing Yang, Mingli Liu, Xiaolong Chen, Cheng Zhang, Huage Liu, Shishan Dong
pmc-12729644.description: Simple SummaryUnderstanding the air quality inside modern chicken houses is essential for protecting both animal health and the well-being of farm workers. In winter, poultry farms often reduce ventilation to maintain warmth, which unintentionally allows airborne bacteria to build up.

pmc-12855888.title: Exploring the impact of digital technology, circular technology and public management on environmental sustainability in emerging economies
pmc-12855888.creator: Yifang Wei, Muhammad Sibt e Ali, Mohd Abass Bhat
pmc-12855888.description: Environmental degradation significantly hampers economic sustainability by causing severe economic problems, prompting researchers to focus on environmental sustainability. Global economies aim to achieve net-zero emissions by 2060 to address climate change issues. Achieving this by 2050 depends on the transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy. Recently, the circular economy (CE) has emerged as a key concept for expediting sustainability.

pmc-12990134.title: Relearning the epistemology, history, and future of neuropsychiatry
pmc-12990134.creator: Juan Camilo Castro Martínez, Felipe Botero-Rodríguez, Jesús Ramírez-Bermúdez, Vaughan Bell, Gabriel Oviedo-Lugo, José Manuel Santacruz-Escudero, Ángela Iragorri, Joan Camprodon, Brian Lawlor, Hernando Santamaría-García
pmc-12990134.description: Neuropsychiatry is a transdisciplinary field at the intersection of neuroscience, psychiatry, neurology, and humanities. Despite this strategic position, a comprehensive framework is still needed to bridge these domains. This review examines the historical evolution of how neurological, mental, and neuropsychiatric symptoms have been conceptualized, from antiquity to contemporary models, using the brain–body dilemma as a guiding thread.

pmc-13066991.title: Corylin inhibits liver cancer cell growth through the endogenous apoptosis and mitophagy
pmc-13066991.creator: Renshuang Zhao, Xin Wang, Mingming Cao, Yaru Li, Shanzhi Li, Zhiru Xiu, Yilong Zhu, Yiquan Li
pmc-13066991.description: BackgroundCorylin is a bioactive extract of Psoralea corylifolia L. with reported antioxidant, anti-tumor, and anti-inflammatory effects. Its anti-tumor effects have been investigated, but mechanistic explanations are lacking. This study mainly focuses on the role and mechanism of Corylin in inducing liver cancer cell death.

pmc-13108008.title: Serum neurofilament light chain levels in patients with small-fiber neuropathy
pmc-13108008.creator: Daniela Noa Zohar, Daria Keren, Lamis Qassim, Mailam Eltity, Efrat Shavit-Stein, Joab Chapman, Amir Dori
pmc-13108008.description: Background:Serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) levels are an increasingly employed tool for the assessment of active axonal injury in a variety of neurological disorders including polyneuropathy. Injury to the small nerve fibers can lead to small fiber neuropathy (SFN), a neurological condition which is clinically manifested by combination of burning pain, various sensory disturbances and symptoms of autonomic dysfunction.

pmc-13302404.title: Prevalence and characteristics of the catecholamine induced QT prolongation syndrome
pmc-13302404.creator: J Gourraud, M Bordet, J Mansourati, A Rajalu, V Cotard, A Thollet, V Probst
pmc-13302404.description: BackgroundWe have recently described large families of idiopathic ventricular fibrillation characterised by catecholamine-induced QT interval prolongation (CIQTP). The patient presented with a normal QT duration at rest but an abnormal QT prolongation (>-11ms) during a mental stress test (MST).ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to investigate the role of this new syndrome in inherited arrhythmic diseases.
